all_found.desc: [ADVISORY] Fresh mutation evidence supersedes a freshness row only when blocksHere, so an orphaned child freshness row (child branch squash-merged and deleted), which epic-ready reads across branches, can no longer be superseded by a fresh child task-done. In enforce mode epic-ready keeps blocking on it until an override; before #178 the re-run superseded it.

[ADVISORY] Some tests obtain an unknown scope by running real git in t.TempDir() and assume it is not inside a git repository. With TMPDIR inside a checkout they fail (the scope becomes known); fine on standard CI.

findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The pr-ready command/skill docs say another branch's open findings do not block this one after git switch, but a branch stacked on A still blocks on A's findings through the range leg. A user stacking B on A expects B to be clear of A's findings; ARCHITECTURE explains the stacked case but these docs contradict it.

[ADVISORY] ARCHITECTURE says a granted override that gates the branch absorbs a re-raise, omitting the readable-scope condition added in 8c87f62. Docs and code disagree for a named run with an unreadable scope.

[ADVISORY] No test pins that the fallback refresh re-stamps no named row's branch; the mutant making the re-stamp unconditional survives. A regression could erase a named row's branch on a fallback run, silently widening its blocking.
